Nov 8 : Luca Van Assche fell short in his bid to become the first French winner of the Paris Masters since 2008, but he will take plenty of positives from a strong run which ended in a semi-final defeat by world number four Ben Shelton. Van Assche, ranked 47th in the world, pushed Shelton hard and took the first set in Saturday's semi-final, before eventually losing 5-7 6-3 6-4 to the American in front of home fans. "It is true that this week is very important for me because I have a lot of high-level matches under my belt in a row. I played Shelton, who is number four in the world," the 22-year-old told reporters after his defeat. "That showed everything that I could do well, where I have some room for progress. This will help me to have more self-confidence, I know now that I can reach a semi-final.

"I know that I can go toe-to-toe with a player like Shelton today. So there is a lot of positive things to get from this, and I will try to work more to be even better next year." Van Assche's run in Paris means he will rise to a career-high ranking of 34th in the world when the latest rankings are published on Monday. Asked if he was aiming to be among the seeded players at next year's Australian Open in January, he said: "I don't think I'm going to think along those lines. "Of course it helps being a seeded player. I will be 34 in the ranking. "It's a very good ranking. It's very positive. But above all, I will try to remain focused on my game, on learning new skills, on progressing, and then the ranking will follow." Shelton will face seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz of Spain in the Paris Masters final later on Sunday.

Nov 8 : Usman Khawaja on Sunday denied that he had "thrown anyone under the bus", a day after an excerpt from the former Australian cricketer's autobiography claimed the entire team had been aware of ball-tampering during a 2018 tour of South Africa. The scandal, dubbed "Sandpapergate" over Australia's scuffing of the ball with sandpaper in the March 2018 test in Cape Town, sparked a major integrity crisis for Cricket Australia. However, only captain Steve Smith and batsmen David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, who was caught with the sandpaper in his pocket, were banned for their part in the scandal. In a video posted on Instagram, Khawaja, who released the excerpt of his autobiography on Saturday, said he had wanted to "come clean" about the incident since 2018.

"I haven't thrown anyone under the bus," added the 39-year-old, who retired from international cricket in January. "The guys that are currently in the team right now and the other people that were there on the South African tour, including me, we're not the victims. "These three guys (Bancroft, Warner and Smith) took the blame for all of us, and they're the victims." Khawaja said he had spoken with the three players involved in "Sandpapergate", and that he had promised Warner he would share his side of the story. "These three guys deserve justice. And I haven't pointed fingers at anyone," he added. "I'm still searching for what I was searching all those years ago for us — me included — to take the blame together as a team so we can all move on from this once and for all." Australia's test side returned to South Africa for the first time since 2018 last month and were beaten 2-1 by the hosts in the three-match series, which was overshadowed in part by discussions of the scandal and the upcoming release of Khawaja's book.

EDINBURGH, Nov 8 : The New Zealand pair of Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan could miss next weekend's Nations Championship clash with Wales, after they picked up injuries at Murrayfield against Scotland on Saturday. Jordan suffered a suspected hamstring injury in the second half of the All Blacks’ convincing 43-21 victory, while Barrett was taken off for a head injury assessment (HIA) which he failed. He had a clash with Scotland substitute Blair Kinghorn. "Jordie failed his HIA, so it’s not sure whether he’ll be available this week, but we’ll get a bit of clarity later,” the All Blacks coach Dave Rennie said. On Jordan, who is the All Blacks’ leading all-time try-scorer, the coach added: “He might have tweaked a hamstring. We’ll assess that, and I’m not sure of the severity of it.”

New Zealand are already without several key players, including inspirational loose forward Ardie Savea, for their four-match November programme in Britain, but had little problem shrugging off the Scottish challenge, even though their hosts were within three points at halftime. “It was an ill-disciplined first half with a couple of yellow cards,” said Rennie of his team, who had both Wallace Sititi and Peter Lakai sent to the sin-bin. “You give Scotland opportunities near finish zone, they're going to hit you, but we were better in the second half.  “We went to a contestable kick game to limit their time from a counterattack point of view, and were a lot more clinical, and we dominated territory a bit better. “You just saw us lose our shape a couple of times, and from turnover we had two or three really gilt-edge opportunities that we spilt,” added the coach. PARIS, Nov 8 : France's Tom Laperche clinched victory in the Route du Rhum's Ultim class in his first appearance, mastering a transatlantic race that knocked out three rival boats. The 29-year-old skipper crossed the finish line in Pointe-a-Pitre at 10:31 p.m. on Saturday (0231 GMT on Sunday) aboard SVR-Lazartigue, completing the 3,542-nautical-mile race from Saint-Malo to Guadeloupe in 6 days, 13 hours, 27 minutes and 40 seconds. He set a race record, beating Charles Caudrelier's 2022 mark of 6 days, 19 hours, 47 minutes and 25 seconds. "I've always seen incredible images of finishes here, of great champions over the decades," Laperche said after his victory.

"My dream, first of all, was to one day sail these boats, perhaps to do some solo sailing, and why not race the Route du Rhum? So to win it at the helm of the most beautiful of the boats in the 2026 edition makes me very, very happy." Laperche, who won the Fastnet Race and the Transat Cafe L'Or last year, was locked in an intense battle with Armel Le Cleac'h in the early part of the race. But the skipper of Maxi Banque Populaire XI eventually capsized off the Azores on Wednesday morning, three days after the start. Le Cleac'h, winner of the 2016-17 Vendee Globe, was rescued by a Panamanian cargo ship. He was not the only one to abandon in the Ultim class, whose trimarans are 32 metres long and 23 metres wide (105 feet by 75 feet). Defending champion Charles Caudrelier was forced out on Tuesday due to foil damage on his new Maxi Edmond de Rothschild — Gitana 18. Anthony Marchand, skipper of Actual Ultim 4, also dropped out of the transatlantic race on Wednesday, two days after suffering a major technical problem with his central rudder. The retirements left the way clear for Laperche, one of the most talented skippers of his generation, who has been mentored by 2012-13 Vendee Globe winner François Gabart. The Ultims were the first boats to finish. The IMOCAs — 60-foot (18-metre) monohulls used in the Vendee Globe and the Ocean Race — are expected to reach Guadeloupe on Tuesday, with MACSF skipper Corentin Horeau leading the fleet.

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK, Nov 7 : Inter Miami's Lionel Messi became the first to win MLS' Golden Boot in back-to-back seasons, the league said on Saturday, the final day of the regular season. • Messi scored a league-high 26 goals across 31 matches, while FC Dallas forward Petar Musa followed with 22 goals and Nashville SC's Sam Surridge recorded 21. • He had 29 goals the previous season, becoming the second in league history to score at least 25 times in back-to-back years. • The 39-year-old Argentine retired from international football earlier this year after 21 years but signed a contract extension with the MLS club through 2028 in October. • The MLS Cup Playoffs begin on November 19. Inter Miami finished the regular season second in the Eastern Conference.

MEXICO CITY, Nov 7 : Nikola Jokic did not need a triple-double to win over Mexico City, just 19 points, 13 rebounds and an arena chanting "MVP." The three-time NBA Most Valuable Player added eight assists as the Nuggets held off a second-half surge from Indiana to win 114-102 on Saturday before a sellout crowd of more than 20,000 at Arena CDMX. "It was a really good crowd. The energy was there the whole game. I didn't know who they were cheering or if it was just for us, but the energy was the most important thing," Jokic told reporters. The game, played during Day of the Dead week for the third consecutive year, was packed with Pacers yellow jerseys, yet much of the noise seemed to be for the Serbian center.

"I think basketball is a global sport, and I think it's really good to travel as a team all over the world. I think it's really nice to see the love from the fans that are supporting us... Mexican people are really emotional, really passionate about whatever they're doing," Jokic said. Before tip-off, Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon addressed the crowd in Spanish: "Vamos Nuggets. Viva Mexico." It was the first Mexico City appearance for either team. The Pacers had never played in Mexico, and the Nuggets had appeared in the country once, a 2006 pre-season game against Golden State in Monterrey. It was the 35th NBA game played in Mexico, including 16 regular-season and 19 pre-season games. The Pacers were without All-Star guard Tyrese Haliburton, who missed the trip with a hamstring strain, blunting a game marketed around him and Jokic. Denver controlled most of the first half, building a lead of as many as 27 on the way to a 64-41 halftime edge. Indiana roared back with a 37-point third quarter and pulled within 102-95 with 7:27 left, but Denver answered. Jamal Murray found a cutting Spencer Jones under the basket, and the Nuggets restored a double-digit cushion. Cameron Johnson added 18 points and Murray had 16 points and eight assists for Denver. Jones, making his season debut after missing the first seven games with a hamstring injury, scored 13 off the bench. Pascal Siakam led Indiana with 23 points and Larry Nance Jr. added 15, tying a career best with five 3-pointers. Former NBA players Danilo Galliari, Nene Hilario, Greivis Vasquez and Horacio Llamas, the first Mexican-born player in the NBA, were recognized between quarters. Denver improved to 5-3, while Indiana fell to 3-7. The Nuggets play at Houston on Monday night.

Source: Reuters

Nov 7 : Elena Rybakina's withdrawal from the WTA Finals on the eve of the season-ending championships is disappointing, but the world number one needs time to recover from the physical toll of a demanding year, tournament director Garbine Muguruza said. Defending champion Rybakina pulled out of the tournament on Saturday, saying she was not physically ready to compete, leaving Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk to take her place in the eight-player field at Indian Wells. Tournament organizers later said a viral illness was the official reason for the withdrawal.    Muguruza, the former world number one and two-time Grand Slam champion, said she had spoken with Rybakina and that the Kazakh had been unable to recover in time after struggling with physical problems late in the season. "We love Elena and we know that she was feeling so-so in Tokyo as well," Muguruza told Reuters. "I spoke to her today and she really couldn't recover on time.

"What we want is for her to feel good, to go rest, to recover. We don't want her to feel like she has to play — only if she's ready to." Rybakina, who won two Grand Slam titles this year, also withdrew from the Tokyo quarter-finals last month because of a neck injury. 'AMAZING FIELD' Rybakina's absence deprives the event of some star power, but Muguruza said the round-robin format and depth of the field would ensure a high-quality tournament. "We have the best players," said Muguruza, who triumphed at the WTA Finals in Guadalajara in 2021.  "I know our world number one is not going to be able to play, but we have an amazing field, the very best. "Every match could be a Grand Slam final. You really need to be ready. You cannot give one inch." Kostyuk, who is making her WTA Finals debut after a breakthrough season that included the Madrid title and a rise into the top 10, was already in Indian Wells as an alternate and practicing when Rybakina withdrew. Muguruza said the Ukrainian, known for her signature post-match backflip celebrations, had earned her opportunity. "Marta is great. She's had a breakthrough year," Muguruza said. "With this year, we have many first-time players in the Finals, and that's very exciting. It's very hard to qualify." Kostyuk has been outspoken about Russia's invasion of Ukraine and does not shake hands with Russian or Belarusian opponents. Muguruza said the tournament would support players in making their own decisions. "They're free to do whatever they feel," she said. "We are open and supporting them." OPPORTUNITY FOR SABALENKA  Rybakina's withdrawal could create an opening for world number two Aryna Sabalenka to make inroads in the rankings.  Sabalenka, who won the Indian Wells title earlier this year, has the chance to reduce the gap with Rybakina at the top of the rankings, Muguruza said, while also highlighting Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva as a player comfortable in the California desert. "Of course, Aryna might be thinking that this can be a good opportunity," Muguruza said. The WTA moved the Finals to Indian Wells from Riyadh, with Muguruza saying player safety had been the decisive consideration amid conflict in the region. "It clearly felt no longer safe to be in a region where there is conflict," she said. "Taking care of the players and looking ahead to what could be safe, comfortable and secure, relocating felt the best decision." Muguruza said players had responded positively to the switch to Indian Wells, where she competed regularly during her career. "When we knew that Indian Wells could be the next venue, it was just a joy," she said, adding that ticket sales have been strong. "The whole thing is just perfect."

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Ferrari teammates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc said they had put last weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix controversy behind them after holding talks aimed at easing tensions following their opening-lap clash. The pair met with team principal Frederic Vasseur this week after their battle derailed Ferrari's hopes of a one-two finish and prompted Hamilton to publicly criticise the way the race unfolded. Vasseur said on Friday that the discussions had been productive and that Ferrari had "turned the page", while Hamilton had insisted earlier in the week that he would not apologise for speaking openly about his frustrations. After qualifying for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Saturday, both drivers struck a conciliatory tone and said the matter was now closed.

"From my perspective, I was very straightforward, of course, and I think it was good to speak," Leclerc told reporters at Interlagos about the incident which he felt had been blown out of proportion. The Monegasque, who became a father this week, said the timing of the discussions had been affected by personal commitments but that talking face-to-face had helped resolve the issue. "Now I consider that a closed chapter, and I think it will be important to look ahead," he said. Hamilton echoed that view, saying the conversation had allowed both drivers to air their perspectives before moving on. "We sat and spoke and we squashed it and we're moving on," the seven-times world champion said. "I think we still have a huge amount of respect for each other. I'm glad we had a chat and now we move on. We've been getting along just fine as normal." The Briton added that neither side had made demands during the talks and that the focus had been on working together more effectively. Leclerc was fourth fastest in qualifying but will drop 10 places on the grid for Sunday's race because of power unit changes, while Hamilton will start from the back after accumulating engine penalties totalling 65 places, prompting Ferrari to stop his participation after the first phase of qualifying.

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Brazilian drivers endured a torrid, rain-hit qualifying session for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Saturday as Gabriel Bortoleto finished last and F1 debutant Rafael Camara qualified 13th, dampening the excitement surrounding Brazil's first home driver pairing at Interlagos in a decade. Audi's Bortoleto slid into the barriers in Q1, reviving memories of last year's nightmare when he retired on the opening lap of his first home Grand Prix after an earlier sprint crash. "Right now, (it feels like) shit. I mean,. what can I say? Last year, I had a crash. This year, I couldn't do qualifying properly because I messed up. "So yeah, it looks like home race for me hasn't been good yet," Bortoleto told reporters, adding he would clear his head and try to put together a strong performance on Sunday.

Camara, making his Formula One debut for Haas after replacing Frenchman Esteban Ocon, spun in Q1 and recovered, only to lose control later in the session and hit the wall. Camara described it as a chaotic qualifying session but played down the incident, saying the support from the home crowd helped him keep a positive mindset despite the setback. "I think it’s another learning experience for tomorrow. Of course, it’s not ideal, but you end up understanding more and preparing yourself much better." Both Brazilians gained places on the grid after qualifying, as penalties reshuffled the starting order. Max Verstappen, Sergio Perez and Lewis Hamilton were already set to start from the back after taking additional power unit components, promoting Bortoleto to 19th. Charles Leclerc, who qualified ahead of Camara, will also drop behind the Brazilian due to a penalty, leaving the Haas driver set to start 11th.

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : George Russell raged over the radio after the Mercedes driver was thwarted in a bid for a morale-boosting fastest lap in Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying on Saturday. Russell carried a five-place grid penalty for an engine change but the Briton still wanted to finish the session on top. Instead, he was told to back off after coming up behind Williams' Alex Albon and the rain then denied him any further chance of beating the pole time set by McLaren's Lando Norris. "Mate, you told me to back off! What the hell?," Russell shouted over the radio after realising his day was done and he was only second fastest and would be seventh on the grid. "P2. I don't want to be P2. I want to be P1."

Team boss Toto Wolff said it was a 50-50 call and Russell, after so many ups and downs this season, had been in league of his own. "I don't think it would have been enough for pole, but he drove perfectly all session and merited to be on pole," said the Austrian of the aborted lap. "He deserved it but you can't make that call. It's 50 per cent right or wrong. Russell's teammate Kimi Antonelli clinched the title at the previous race in Mexico City and the Briton is now fourth in the battle for overall runner-up after starting the season as title favourite. "That was definitely the pole lap," the 28-year-old said later. "Misjudgement on our side. Need to understand what happened as obviously the rain was coming and we should have just finished the lap. "It depends on the weather," he said of his prospects on Sunday. "I mean, I felt good out there. It's the first time in a while I've felt confident in the car. I felt more confident in the wet than I do in the dry, I don't really understand why that was. "I felt more like myself... unfortunately when it mattered we didn't execute." Russell took the first win of his F1 career at Interlagos in 2022. McLaren team boss Andre Stella acknowledged that the Briton was "probably the fastest car" in the third phase of qualifying. "I saw that he was not impeded, but he just found Albon, and he couldn't close his second lap on inters, which I think up until that point was on par with pole position, if not faster," Stella told reporters.
